chunk_findings.detail: The new `partial` branch calls `GA.refusal(it, gate)`, but `_no_tree_reason`’s item parameter is `item` — the surrounding f-strings and the pre-existing final return all interpolate `{item}`, and no `it` name is defined in this function. For the exact merged-partial case this change is meant to handle, Python raises `NameError: name 'it' is not defined` before the partial-preserving return can be produced, so the bug is not fixed and the gate advice crashes.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gates/_tree.py:173

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion `assert "ddflow approve" not in text` still over-constrains a correct message for a hand-recorded, non-baseline-red partial. A truthful message such as ``ddflow approve does not accept this partial; only a person's re-record of unit_tests can settle it`` satisfies the intended behavior and makes no false approve or passed-record offer, but it contains the forbidden substring and this test fails. The triage fixed only the analogous `gate record`/`--outcome passed` guard and did not answer this half of the earlier finding.

data.body:
Fixes bug Bae7ae3e86c: ddflow merge fails transiently with 'fatal: Could not read from .git/MERGE_MSG: No such file or directory' in the primary (seen 2026-11-08 merging fix-B-merged-partial-rerun-records-unavailable, branch 117 behind main); _merge_retrying_stash retries ONLY 'fatal: stash failed', so this error is not retried and the first merge spuriously fails — an immediate manual retry succeeded (8a652ef08679). Signal: extend the retry to this error too.

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-Bae7ae3e86c --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed Bae7ae3e86c --regression-test <test>` first).
